what: Which token set is which, and which run used which. Written because not knowing cost two training runs.
why: train/run.py defaults --tokens-dir to artifacts/tokens. That default is the OLDEST corpus in the directory. Two v0.77.0 runs were launched without the flag and compared against a baseline trained on a different corpus; the resulting ~1.3 nat 'gap' was nearly attributed to beta2 0.95 and nearly cost a working config.

token_sets.note: The DEFAULT --tokens-dir, and the oldest. This is the trap.
The frozen EVALUATION set used by scripts/evaluate.py comparisons, which is a separate role from training data.
THE DIALOGUE CORPUS. Built seven minutes before checkpoints-1024-dialogue's first checkpoint. This is what the current designated model trained on, and what any comparison against it must use.

how_tokens-v4_was_identified: By mtime against the baseline's checkpoint timestamps, corroborated by throughput: the dialogue run reached step 2000 in about six minutes, which requires ddp 4 at ~5.3 it/s, and a matched ddp-4 rerun reproduces that rate. No run log survives for that baseline -- only val_losses.jsonl -- which is itself the underlying problem.
the_actual_lesson: A run that does not record its own --tokens-dir cannot be compared to anything later. checkpoints-1024-dialogue has no train.log; checkpoints-ts10-b-s5489 does, which is the only reason its config was knowable at all.
suggested_fix: train/run.py should write a run manifest into --checkpoint-dir next to val_losses.jsonl: tokens dir and token counts, resolved optimizer block, seed, ddp, steps, batch, seq_len, tt-metal version. Not implemented yet.
